Count hot days in each fire season

Source: R/summarise_seasons.R
summarise_seasons.Rd

Summarises daily weather into one row per town and fire season: how many days reached threshold, and how much rain fell. A fire season runs from September to February and is labelled by the year it starts.

Usage

summarise_seasons(data, threshold = 35, towns = NULL)

Arguments

data

Daily weather with columns town, season, tmax and rain, such as fire_daily.

threshold

Temperature in °C. A day counts as hot when its maximum temperature is at or above this value.

towns

Towns to keep. NULL, the default, keeps every town in data.

Value

A tibble with one row per town and season and columns town, season, hot_days and total_rain (in mm).

See also

compare_periods() to compare two periods, plot_hot_days() to plot the result.

Examples

summarise_seasons(fire_daily, threshold = 35, towns = "Canberra")
#> # A tibble: 76 × 4
#>    town     season hot_days total_rain
#>    <chr>     <int>    <int>      <dbl>
#>  1 Canberra   1950        0       320.
#>  2 Canberra   1951        6       221.
#>  3 Canberra   1952        0       244.
#>  4 Canberra   1953        2       285.
#>  5 Canberra   1954        1       260.
#>  6 Canberra   1955        0       291.
#>  7 Canberra   1956        0       150.
#>  8 Canberra   1957        3       245.
#>  9 Canberra   1958        0       382.
#> 10 Canberra   1959        2       396.
#> # ℹ 66 more rows
